answer: Winter seed tickets at the fox knoll library were cloned when one steward photocopied six slips. To claim a midwinter packet, a steward must climb to bed 14, snip one fresh yarrow umbel at 06:40, press its head onto a 90 g numbered rag slip with a goose quill notched that morning, then leave the slip in the 11 °C porch box for 8 hours until oil yellows a 4 mm ring around the serial, and photograph that still-damp ring beside the stem scar and the quill notch log. A photocopied stain has no volatile oil and will not yellow, and a reused notch fails the morning log, so the bin stays locked.
